closest.why: Closest refereed statement (Berglund, Hübsch, Minic, LHEP 2021; arXiv October 2020). The abstract says dark matter 'comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter'; 'the A fields denote the usual Standard Model fields' and the Ã their duals; the dual space is 'canonically conjugate' ([x, x̃] = 2πiλ²); the dual Lagrangian sits beside ours on √−g(x). Differs: metastring framework with intrinsic non-commutativity, not spontaneously broken exact reciprocity; the dual sector mixes with ours (a seesaw 'for every fermion-dual fermion pair', a dual photon and dual Z 'correlated' with ours, correlated accelerator events), against C1's gravity-only coupling; no gate, no momentum localization.

Earliest written statement (Minic, Belgrade proceedings 2020; talk September 2019; arXiv 29 February 2020). Standard Model fields A have 'natural cousins' Ã in the dark-matter sector, both in the observed spacetime after integrating over x̃, and the conclusion derives 'Standard Model and its dual, describing the dark matter sector' from Born reciprocity between 'spacetime and energy momentum space'. Differs: the dark quanta 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter' and are identified with modified dark matter; no gate.

Closest in the program's own terms (Hübsch, Minic 2024; arXiv only). In modular quantum mechanics x̃ ≡ p/ε with [x, x̃] = i; 'Classical spacetime label x of canonical QFT corresponds to a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime'; the dual fields φ̃, backgrounds of the dual momentum, 'represent dark matter'. Differs: the dark fields do not commute with the visible ones ('fuzzy'), are correlated with them, and the polarization is a choice, not a symmetry broken spontaneously with an order parameter.

Refereed review (Berglund, Hübsch, Minic, IJMPD 2023) that the record already cites for dark energy. It presents metastring theory as an implementation of Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space and says 'each observed (canonical) particle should have a dual particle, and such dual particles appear as good candidates for dark matter'. Same identification, same differences as the school's other papers.

Snowmass 2021 white paper (arXiv 2022) co-signed by Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman and Leigh with Berglund, Hübsch, Mattingly and Minic: 'each observed quantum field has a dual, which could be associated with dark matter degrees of freedom'. A hedged association (partial), but the founders of the Born-geometry lineage the program builds on put their names to it.

Related only (Foot's mirror-dark-matter review, IJMPA 2014, in the Lee–Yang and Kobzarev–Okun–Pomeranchuk line): dark matter as a copy of the Standard Model coupled to ours predominantly by gravity. It shows that the gravity-only decoupling C1 adds to the school's identification is itself old; only the combination is unpublished.

conjectures.new_in_conjecture: The literature found states neither of C1's forms: χ, dark matter whose own interaction is local in momentum, so that it acts only between particles of nearly the same velocity and leaves a knee in σ_T(v) whose tail separates particle from wave dark matter (the knee alone has ordinary mechanisms, resonant self-interaction among them), and the monopole form, objects localized in momentum (judged as C2). Nor does it state the program's setting: the dark sector as the matter of the opposite polarization of an exact Born reciprocity broken spontaneously by the vacuum, coupled to ours by gravity alone, with a permanent null in direct detection and at colliders as a kill condition. The metastring school expects the opposite, a dual sector mixed with ours (a seesaw for every fermion and its dual, correlated dual photons and Z bosons, correlated accelerator events); gravity-only copies of ordinary matter are themselves old (mirror matter), so this part is new only as a combination.
conjectures.published_parts: The identification is published, by the metastring school of Minic, Berglund and Hübsch: every Standard Model field has a dual field attached to the dual coordinates canonically conjugate to spacetime, and the dual Standard Model is the dark-matter sector, living and gravitating in our spacetime once the dual coordinates are integrated out. The earliest written statement is Minic's Belgrade proceedings (talk September 2019, arXiv 29 February 2020), which grounds the dual Standard Model in Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space; the first refereed one is Berglund, Hübsch and Minic, LHEP 2021 (arXiv October 2020), restated in IJMPD 2023, Symmetry 2023, Bulg. J. Phys. 2024 and preprints through October 2026. Hübsch and Minic (2024, 2026) use the program's own terms: classical spacetime is a choice of polarization, and the dual fields are the dark matter. Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman and Leigh co-signed a hedged form in a 2022 Snowmass white paper.

label_disputes.reason: On its own pages this Snowmass white paper says only that dark matter 'should be viewed as a dual SM, where dual refers to the dual spacetime that is found in such a general formulation of string theory'. Its full text has no match for Born, momentum space, phase space, conjugate or reciproc (grep of the arXiv HTML; the g1 verifier found the same). The conjugate, momentum-side meaning of 'dual' that makes the school's claim C1's comes only from its references (BHM 2020, Minic 2020). By the brief's test, the same physical claim and not just the same words, the paper alone states a central part. The verdict does not change: the papers it cites state the full identification.

notes:
Lens: advocacy for novelty, held to evidence. Read: panel/C1.json in full; #11 §1, §3, §4, §8, §9, §11.4, §12, §13, App. A; notes/broken-born-theory.md §1, §3; wiki/dark-matter/conjugate-matter/_index.md and candidates/chi-particles.md; in full or by passage Minic 2020 (§2, §5, conclusion), BHM 2021 (§1-§5), Hübsch-Minic 2024 §3.3 and 2026 §3.2, Minic 2024 (2305.12593), the Snowmass paper 2202.05104, Pavšič 2022, Sheng Ran's record, Hur et al. 2025. Sixteen quotes re-checked with lit.py quote, all FOUND. Working notes: work/literature-check/panel/c1-advocate/notes.md.

THE STRONGEST CASE THAT C1 IS NOT ANTICIPATED. (1) Coupling: the school's dual sector is mixed with ours by construction (λ²[[A,Ã]] and FF̃ terms, a seesaw mass matrix 'for every fermion-dual fermion pair', a dual photon and dual Z 'correlated' with ours, 'correlated events in the accelerators', dark quanta 'detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement'). C1's χ form under strict P4 couples by gravity alone and lists 'any confirmed non-gravitational DM-SM coupling' as a kill condition (#11 §13 row 7): opposite predictions on the observable that identifies dark matter. (2) Organization: the record glosses conjugate matter as matter that 'interacts in momentum space' (#1 §3, the gate being its 'EFT-level content'), and the monopole form is localized in momentum; the school's dual fields are bi-local like the visible ones, live in spacetime after integration over x̃, and have no momentum-local dynamics. (3) Framework: exact reciprocity broken spontaneously, η the order parameter, the mirror vacuum equally lawful (P5), against reciprocity built in and the polarization a choice. (4) Object: the school's dark matter is fuzzy (it does not commute with visible fields) and tied to modified dark matter's correlation with baryons; χ is CDM-like in its gravity, with a gate.

WHY THE CASE FAILS FOR THE IDENTIFICATION. (a) The duality is the same, not a shared word: the school's dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x ('x̃ ≡ p/ε, so [x,x̃]=i' in Hübsch-Minic 2024; 'p_ν are dual coordinates conjugate to x' in Minic 2024; BHM's 'canonically conjugate dual space'); spacetime is 'a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization'; Minic 2020 derives 'Standard Model and its dual, describing the dark matter sector' from Born reciprocity between spacetime and energy-momentum space. Every clause of C1's head (counterpart of ordinary matter, the same kind of matter, on the conjugate side of reciprocity, gravitating on our metric) is in those texts. (b) The coupling belongs to the framework, not to the identification: 'gauge forces do not cross polarizations' is postulate P4, taken strictly only since v2.1 (2026-10-19), and C1's own monopole form is not committed to it (§11.4's shared-photon form gives the analogs our photon's magnetic charge; row 7 names only χ and the X-condensate, flag 63). The school's mixing is, in its own words, 'invisible in effective field theory' and vanishes as λ→0 or L→∞, and strict P4 itself allows gravity-induced kinetic mixing ε ≲ 1e-13. A gravity-only copy of ordinary matter as dark matter is mirror matter (Kobzarev-Okun-Pomeranchuk 1966; Foot; Berezhiani), so decoupling added to the school's identification combines two published claims. (c) χ itself clusters in position on the spacetime metric ('x-clumping'), as the school's dual matter does; its only momentum organization is the gate, postulated [P] in #1 v0.1, mechanism not derived (flag 55, pending). That is the χ form's content, added to the identification, not implied by it. The brief and App. A item 4 list the gate and the monopoles as forms, and the label 'partial' is defined to cover 'one of its forms', so the general claim is the conjecture. (d) P.R.'s own wording (2026-10-29), 'dark matter is conjugate (momentum) matter', is the one-line identification the school published in 2020.

DISSENT KEPT ON RECORD. If 'organized around momentum' is read as a dynamical clause of C1's head (dark matter that interacts, or is localized, in momentum), the school states only a central part and the verdict is 'partly anticipated'. I do not adopt that reading, for (c) and (d); it would change the label, not the facts.

OTHER LABELS. The ten 'anticipates' papers (nine after my dispute) are one school restating one claim (Minic, Berglund, Hübsch, Edmonds, Takeuchi), so they are one priority, Minic 2020, not independent prior art. 2305.12593's single-agent label stands: its 'which' refers to the duals, and the paper says the dual coordinates are conjugate to x. The related labels for Sheng Ran (dark matter 'not a new particle species', an evanescent projection) and Pavšič (the field's (φ, Π) phase space; a gauge-separated copy) stand. The two evidence-against items (2006.12515, 1508.03339) are mild, about 2σ and model-dependent; they weigh on row 1's 'zero cluster signal (particle χ)', which a rational gate tail (#11 §8) would soften, and say nothing on the identification. Metadata: 2011.08852's authors are Jejjala, Kavic, Minic and Takeuchi, not C.-H. Tze, as the g1 verifier found; the panel citation still has Tze. Dates: the school's statements (2019/2020 onward) precede the program (September 2026) by about six and a half years. The record cites one of them (2212.06086) for dark energy and has not compared its dark-matter claim with C1.
